you relish exceptionally punishing and obscure gameplay

★★★★★ 10/10
I bought Cruelty Squad because the screenshots looked like malware.
I refunded it after 20 minutes.
Then I bought it again.
Then I started explaining its economic systems to my friends like a conspiracy theorist standing in front of a wall covered in red string.
Cruelty Squad is one of those games that actively hates you for existing. Not in the modern "hard but fair" sense. Not in the "prepare to die" sense. It hates your eyes. It hates your ears. It hates your expectations. It hates every lesson the videogame industry has spent the last twenty years teaching players.
The menus look broken.
The UI looks infected.
The textures look like they were recovered from a cursed hard drive found in a landfill behind a biotech corporation.
The soundtrack sounds like a panic attack transmitted through a dying modem.
And somehow it's one of the greatest immersive sims ever made.
The first thing most people notice is the graphics. Calling them ugly is missing the point. They're not ugly by accident. They're ugly with malicious intent. The game is trying to create a world so spiritually rotten that every texture feels diseased.
Every environment looks like capitalism reached its final evolutionary stage and immediately developed terminal cancer.
The world of Cruelty Squad is one where human life has become so cheap that death barely matters anymore. Corporations own everything. Morality has been liquidated into a market asset. Assassination is just another gig-economy side hustle.
You aren't the hero.
You aren't the villain.
You're just another disposable employee.
And somehow that's funny.
Very funny.
Disturbingly funny.
The writing constantly bounces between philosophical satire and complete nonsense. One moment you're reading something that feels like a critique of hyper-capitalism, wealth inequality, and corporate dehumanization. The next moment you're buying organ futures and investing in fish. Somehow both systems are equally important to you…

cohorts.label: 2-20h
cohorts.summary: Reviewers highlight the steep learning curve, obscure controls, and complete absence of hand-holding or tutorials.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that reloading requires a specific control input of right-clicking and dragging the mouse down and up.

citations.review_text:
Cruelty Squad is a shining example of why games are art. It is violent, anarchistic and intentionally hostile and unnerving, twisting the concept of a first-person immersive sim into an alien, yet functional direction. The controls are weird, reloading happens by right-clicking and dragging the mouse down and up, but it still works, after a moment of learning. The UI is off-putting but gives all the relevant information. The gameplay is solid: Everything dies basically instantly to any weapon, including the player. The story...

I did not detect a story. In lieu of one, Cruelty Squad is all about vibes, which there are plenty of. Not necessarily pleasant vibes, but vibes still. I'm hesitant to describe it more, since you should experience it firsthand.

I finished all the missions, except for the secret extra ones. And after watching the Civvie11 review, I realized that in order to get the... ultimate? ending, I had to jump through unexplained hoops, with escalating difficulty and bullhonkey. And I had to give up. I could tolerate the game until it forces me to open a wiki to see how the game ends. I don't have patience for that, and I respect anyone who does.

So, if you manage to get to the end, well done, art-appreciator. You deserve a hug.

i bought this for the first time in april, and refunded shortly after. I didn't like the controls back then. Fast forward to today, i bought the game again and oh boy this is fun. I recommend this game to anyone who had even the slightes though of buying this game. Extremely unique mechanics, weapons and artstyle

claims.claim: Reviewers mention that the game features a lack of hand-holding, leaving players to figure out the relentless gameplay or die.

citations.review_text:
this is the game where you can use your intestines as a grappling hook, invest organs and fish into the stock market, fight various godlike beings, obliterate a guy who owns an extensive funkopop collection, throw toxic gas-leaking toilets at people, and re-establishing the balance of life and death in the game's world. the graphics are both nauseating and beautiful, the gameplay is relentless, leaving you to figure it out or die, and the overall plot and lore is deeper than you would think.

this really is like Gorbino's quest. it is the Gorbino's quest of life.
10/10.

(there's also a 4 hour long documentary of the game on youtube. insane.)

Honestly one of the best games i've ever played. I cant even categorize what this game is:D

If you're looking for a game that has a lot of replayability and is actually hard, Cruelty Squad is exactly for you. The missions were interesting and fun with all kinds of different routes, even more with augments. The game tells you "no hand holding" and that's exactly what it does. If you want different and better weapons or secret augments there is no indicator what you should do to get them but when i was really stuck on a mission, i found good help with the community posts and videos, so there is no chance that you wouldn't be able to complete Cruelty Squad. The community is honestly really awesome, so a big shout out for them

My only criticism about the Cruelty Squad is that i wanted more missions and achievements. The game is made by a single dev so i totally understand that it isn't that long, the replayability makes up for it in my opinion. One thing i forgot to mention but the artwork is really cool, dystopian and almost gory. 

Definitely will be waiting for future games by Consumer Softproducts!

claims.claim: Reviewers note that levels feature open-ended design with multiple routes and approaches to objectives.

citations.review_text:
Pros:
-Good movement
-The different ways to get around almost every level gives different playstyles completely different feelings
-Large array of build variety

Cons:
-Specifically designed to look as disgusting as possible
-High, somewhat inconsistent difficulty
-Sometimes hard to navigate

Cruelty Squad is easily one of my favorite games I've ever played.

The first thing that grabbed me was the visual style. It's ugly, bizarre, and completely unapologetic about it, but somehow it all comes together into a really memorable aesthetic. The music and sound design are just as strange and memorable, and they fit the game's atmosphere perfectly.

The gameplay is where the game really shines for me. It's challenging without feeling like it's simply trying to punish you, and learning the mechanics and figuring out how to approach each situation is incredibly satisfying. I especially love the open-ended level design. Missions give you a lot of freedom to experiment, and there are usually multiple ways to approach an objective. You can plan things out, take a completely ridiculous route, or discover some strange interaction that somehow works.

There's a very unique feeling to playing Cruelty Squad that I've never really gotten from another game. Everything about it feels intentionally hostile, weird, and unpredictable, but underneath all of that is a surprisingly deep and rewarding immersive sim.

It's definitely not a game for everyone, but if you can get past the deliberately bizarre presentation, there's an incredible game underneath it. Highly recommended.

I bought this game and it took me like 2-3 months to actually play it, but once I gave it a chance I can confidently say it's one of the best games I've ever played. It's definitely the most unique game I've ever played. Each level in this game is like a puzzle, that can be approached in so many different ways depending on how you choose to play the game. If you're debating on whether or not to buy this game let me just give you some information before you make your decision: This game is hard, you will die a lot which is why you're encouraged to try loads of different approaches and play styles. It is also a very rewarding experience but patience is a necessity when playing this game otherwise you wont enjoy it. I have 100% the game and I can tell you now once you get to the late game after you've already become used to how the game works, you will enjoy the game a lot. Note: if you're just getting this game because of the art style, you'll be in for a nasty surprise when you realise how difficult this game is. In conclusion, get the game if you're up for a challenging but rewarding experience.
To say this game is strange is an understatement and it is the most unique game i've played. However it's also very rich in its design as there are tons of ways to complete the levels.

As of now, I have officially 100% completed Cruelty Squad. Every gun (including the accursed Zippy 3000), every mission from HQ to Trauma Loop has been beaten on Punishment, Chaos, and with the Extravagant Suit, S rank in all categories from every mission, every implant has been bought and found, every fish (from the poolsucker to the soul) has been caught, and every part (even the horrible Rotten Spine, which was the final thing I needed and the hardest thing for me to get) has been acquired. Therefore, I think I am well qualified to make a review on this game.
This game and its creator HATES you, the player. You will be put into pure torment and misery, especially trying to 100% this game. That being said, I love this game. It is truly one of a kind and one of the best immersive shooters of our time. After completing this game, I think I've finally unlocked the CEO mindset, though I don't think ANY real life CEO has worked and struggled this hard. This truly is the Gorbino's Quest of life.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the game features clunky controls.

citations.review_text:
kill your landlord kill your landlord
unironically a fairly good commentary on late stage capitalism disguised as a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, and one of the best examples i know of of video games as an artistic medium. getting thrown into, well, the complete ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ of everything the game throws you into is a great parallel to the themes of ad nauseum optimization and for-profit-ization of everything, it's like if you threw someone from the past from a quaint small medieval town into a buzzing ad-filled flashy metropolitan center
it's a bit clunky to play and takes a while to get used to and it's pretty unfair and the level design is frequently easily cheesable and it's great, surprisingly has a great amount of replay value and there's probably more secret content than there is non-secret content
i wouldn't say it's *good* as a video game but it's great as an interactive artwork and is an incredibly unique experience, if you don't want to play through it yourself (which, to be honest, fair enough) there's some great videos on youtube

It isn't... *good*, at least not in the way that you'd expect a game to be, but it is deeply fascinating and entertaining. This game has clunky controls, bizarre writing, and an abrasive visual/audio design, but it's also funny and unique in ways that are hard to explain. It feels great to steadily improve at levels and discover new ways to play, finding implants is super rewarding. The game kinda grew on our brain like mold, and eventually it ended up becoming one of our favorite games ever. Worth picking up if it's on sale for sure.
